title: Two-step linear images of special quasi-projective groups
exact_target: For every connected smooth special complex quasi-projective variety V, every $d\geq 1$ and every representation $\rho :\pi _{1}(V)\to GL_d(C)$, must its image have a finite-index subgroup nilpotent of class at most two? The assertion concerns representation images, not virtual nilpotence of $\pi _{1}(V)$ itself.
